summary: Claude Code invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "add logging" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-logging-design.md, presented it for review, and only began implementation planning after I approved.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are supported by observed screen text, session-log content, and on-disk files. The router escalated correctly to the architectural path, wrote and surfaced a spec before any code, and only proceeded to planning/implementation after my 'looks good, go ahead'. The Codex gate returning no verdict is a separate defect worth flagging but did not block the scenario.

observations.description: The Codex spec gate produced no verdict: agent reported 'Both round-1 lenses ... returned empty payloads; verdict-normalize scored each incomplete — "json payload has no terminal verdict"' and 'status --json showed no job records at all (running: [], latestFinished: null, recent: [])'. Agent concluded the stub backend is broken. The earlier approach gate failed identically. The spec therefore carries no external sign-off.

The agent silently created a new .gitignore in a repo that had none (covering docs/hyperpowers and docs/superpowers) citing a 'standing instruction'; it did flag it, but adding an unrelated repo-level file during a design phase is surprising.

The brainstorming Q&A was long: six separate AskUserQuestion prompts plus two free-text approval checkpoints before the spec appeared. Each prompt's prose was several screens long, so most of the reasoning had scrolled off before the choice list rendered.

The multi-select tooling question required five Down presses to reach 'Submit' plus a second confirm screen ('Ready to submit your answers?'), which is noticeably clunkier than the single-select prompts.
Claude's startup wizard (theme, security notes, folder-trust, bypass-permissions) still appeared despite the HOWTO stating dialog-bypass state is seeded in the isolated $HOME.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use dump (jq over ade3bcc9-...jsonl) first entry: 'Skill: hyperpowers:brainstorming', preceding all Read/Write calls.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: '**Classification: architectural.** "Logging" is a new subsystem rather than a change to a flow that already exists here, so I'll run the full process — questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec — before any code.' File on disk: ./docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-logging-design.md (find in coding-agent-workdir).

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code written
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-logging-design.md (not committed) ... Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan.' At that moment `find . -type f` in the workdir showed only index.html, README.md, package.json, app.js, src/index.js, src/utils.js, .gitignore and the spec — no logger implementation files.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: grep of assistant text for 'bounded' returned only 'Recovery, bounded:' in the Codex gate report; classification line says 'architectural', and a committed... spec file exists at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-logging-design.md.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: grep -in 'spike' over assistant text returned no classification hits (only 'architectural' and the 'Recovery, bounded' phrase); no probe plan was presented — the agent produced a full sectioned design and spec.
